# Project Overview

This is a Next.js project that integrates TypeScript and TailwindCSS. The application is containerized using Docker (see [`Dockerfile`](./../../docker-context/Dockerfile)).

> [!note]
> Refer to [`package.json`](./../../docker-context/package.json) for the specific versions of the dependencies used in this project. Please ensure the correct syntax and features for the versions used when providing suggestions.

## Project Structure

The project is structured as follows. All the folder and file names are in kebab-case, except for `components/*`:

### `app/`

The routes that follow the Next.js App Router convention.

### `components/`

Reusable components. The components are formed as follows:

- The components are named using PascalCase:
  - `Content*`: Composite components
  - Most of components are named according to their outer element, usually a HeroUI component, e.g., `Card*`, `Button*`, etc.
- `components/*.tsx`: When a component is self-contained
- `components/*/index.tsx`: When a component contains sub-components
- `components/*/*.ts`: Sub-components in the same folder

### `files/`

Markdown and data files served through helper functions:

- `files/articles/`: Markdown files that follow the naming convention of `YYYY-MM-DD.md`, where the filename represents the publication date. The articles use some special front-matter fields and syntaxes (see `getArticleByFilename` in `helpers/server/article.ts` for details)
- `files/documents/`: Other markdown files. Every file has its own formatting and front-matter fields (see `getProfile` in `helpers/server/document.ts` for details). The sections between `<!-- generated:*:start/end -->` markers in `Profile.md` are generated by `scripts/build-profile.mjs` — edit `files/resume/Resume.yaml` instead
- `files/resume/`: The resume source of truth (see [`client-resume.md`](./client-resume.md))

### `helpers/`

Contains functions that can work in both server and client environments. Helpers for the same domain are named using the same filename, e.g., `helpers/article.ts` and `helpers/server/article.ts`. The folder is further divided into:

- `helpers/server/*.ts`: Contains server-only functions
- `helpers/client/*.ts`: Contains client-only functions
- `helpers/*.ts`: Contains functions that can work in both server and client environments

### `public/`

Static assets. While these files can be accessed directly via `/<folder>/<file>` (a Next.js feature), it is fetched using the full URL through helper functions for server-side rendering. The folder structure is as follows:

- `public/images/`: Images used in the website:
  - Article scoped images are stored in `public/images/<YYYY-MM-DD>/` and named in the `Pascal-Case.ext` way, e.g., `public/images/2024-08-19/Branch-Name-LTS.png`

### `scripts/`

Build scripts run through the npm scripts in `package.json`, e.g., `build-static.mjs`, `build-resume.mjs`, and `build-profile.mjs`.

### `settings/`

Configuration files and constants. The folder is split into:

- `settings/config.ts`: Hardcoded data for the home page, which may be shared across multiple components
- `settings/constant.ts`: Global constants used in both server and client environments
- `settings/heads.ts`: Global metadata, viewport, and font configuration for `<head />`
- `settings/icons.ts`: Icon mapping

### `stores/`

Global state management using Zustand. Note that some of the states are parsed before everything is loaded in `components/Entry.tsx`, which is contained in the root layout `app/layout.tsx`.

### `styles/`

Global CSS styles.
